about: Upgrade paths and rollback, one entry per release, oldest first (#221, #222). min_from_version: the oldest release that upgrades directly to this one, applying the steps of every release after it, in order. rollback_without_restore: whether the previous release boots and serves on the control-plane schema and the catalogs this release leaves; when false, rollback_blocked_by says why, and only a restore of the backup taken before the upgrade goes back. The manager reads this file at boot (ReleaseGate) and release_manifest.py copies the release's entry into release.json. changesets: the Liquibase changelog files the release adds. release.sh adds the next release's entry when it moves version.sbt to its snapshot; a pull request adding a changelog file lists it there, and one adding a one-way change (a drop, a rename, a type change, a new NOT NULL, a DuckDB or DuckLake bump that migrates catalogs) sets rollback_without_restore false and says why. release_manifest.py --check-pins refuses a changelog file no entry lists, and a one-way one under rollback_without_restore true.

rollback_blocked_by: Liquibase 0055 drops qodstate_pool.lockdown, which 0.10.x reads: a 0.10.x manager fails at boot with column "lockdown" does not exist

steps.text: Back up the control-plane database: Liquibase 0047 to 0055 run at boot and 0055 is one way.
Replace the static API key with personal access tokens and remove QOD_API_KEY everywhere: a manager ignores it and warns.

Unset QOD_ACL_FILTERED_METADATA and QOD_ACL_DIALECT (refused at any value), and QOD_ACL_ENABLED and QOD_NODE_LOCKDOWN (refused when off), with their quack-flightsql.acl.* and quack-flightsql.nodeLockdown keys.
Grant tenant users what they read: enforcement can no longer be turned off and per-pool lockdown is gone. On OPA tenants, update the policies for the node's input (columns, via, locations).
If users load files, set QOD_TENANT_FILES_ROOT, and list in QOD_USER_S3_ALLOWED_ENDPOINTS any endpoint other than AWS their own S3 keys target.

In fleet mode set QOD_INTERNAL_URL on every manager; on Kubernetes without the chart set QOD_POD_IP. The REST port + 1 must be free, or set QOD_INTERNAL_PORT. Under HA, set QOD_NODE_KEY_SECRET to one value on every replica, or on none.

With the Helm chart, unset env.QOD_INTERNAL_URL, env.QOD_INTERNAL_PORT and env.QOD_POD_IP (helm upgrade fails on them), and size the pod for a 2 GiB heap and 512 MiB of direct memory, or set javaOpts.
Upgrade every HA replica together (scale to one replica or use a Recreate rollout), and upgrade the qod CLI with the manager, on every fleet server too.

Restart every node (node protocol 6); on Kubernetes pull this release's node image. Read the boot log's WARN and ERROR lines about untrusted initSql, sql federation sources and parked clientSecretRef values.
Back up the control-plane database: Liquibase 0056 runs at boot and adds the three-way merge columns to qodstate_branch_merge.
On Kubernetes, read your maintenance policies: a database with maintenance enabled runs it for the first time after this upgrade.
On OPA tenants, a rule keyed on columns no longer refuses a branch's change count, which is asked with columns: []: refuse on the table instead.
Under HA, finish a rolling upgrade before merging a branch.
Propose again any branch proposal made before the upgrade: its merge is refused 409 proposal_stale.
Back up the control-plane database: Liquibase 0057 runs at boot and adds a policy-version trigger on object-store keys.

Give every database whose metastore names another Postgres server its own pgUser and pgPassword (qod database update): QoD's login is no longer filled in there, and such a database stops connecting at its next node start.
Recompile any manager module calling PoolSupervisor.createTenantDb: it now states writerTrusted.
Upgrade the node image and fleet servers with the manager, and restart every node.
Run the manager on Java 25 or later (qod start and qod serve download a Temurin 25 JRE when none is found; run-jar.sh and run-jar.ps1 need JAVA_HOME or java on PATH at 25).
A manager launched with -cp passes --enable-native-access=ALL-UNNAMED and --sun-misc-unsafe-memory-access=allow itself.
Correct any database's defaultSchema or defaultDatabase that is not a plain identifier before its next update or manifest import.
Replace any personal access token that administers QoD under verbCeiling RO: it is now read-only on admin REST and MCP too.
Set QOD_MAINT_RUN_TIMEOUT_MIN above the longest full maintenance chain of your largest database: it now caps the whole chain, and its default rises from 60 to 240 minutes.
Clear any database's defaultDatabase that names another catalog than its own (qod database update --default-database ''): it is ignored, and create and update refuse it.
Under HA, an upgraded leader can fail as stale a maintenance run still executing on a replica of the earlier release; the next tick queues it again.
Upgrade the node image and fleet servers with the manager, and restart every node: until a node restarts, each real authorization outage on it reads as a denial instead of a retryable UNAVAILABLE.

Enable every disabled tenant still in use: from this release a disabled tenant's nodes stop at the first boot and its users can no longer sign in, use their tokens or keep their sessions; only a superuser can enable it again.

If an upgrade agent runs deploy/host/install.sh through sudo with a rule that allows any argument, narrow it to the version argument: install.sh now takes --wheel FILE, which chooses code that runs as root.

rollback_blocked_by: 0061-platform-roles: an older manager treats every tenant-less row, staff users included, as a data-plane superuser

steps.text: Back up the control-plane database: Liquibase 0061 runs at boot, and once staff users exist only a restore of that backup goes back, as an older manager reads every staff user as a superuser.

Unset QOD_ADMIN_KIND (and quack-on-demand.admin.kind) or set it to admin: any other value is refused at boot, as the seeded accounts have no tenant and only kind admin makes a tenant-less account a superuser.

Check that no tenant row has the kind staff (SELECT tenant, username, kind FROM qodstate_user WHERE tenant IS NOT NULL AND lower(kind) = 'staff' returns nothing) and change the kind of any such row first: Liquibase 0061 refuses a staff row with a tenant.

Check third-party manager modules: a module whose public path prefix is malformed, is /api or one segment under it, lies under a core API segment or another module's name, or lies outside /api under none of its own static mounts refuses boot.

On an OPA tenant whose Rego compares catalog, schema, table or column names holding a non-ASCII uppercase letter, update the rules to the new input: names arrive folded as DuckDB folds them, ASCII letters only, and a deny rule written against the old lowercased form stops matching.

Find every stored column policy, row policy and grant whose names hold a non-ASCII letter, and respell each one that does not name its table or column exactly as stored (ASCII case aside): names now match as DuckDB binds them, so from the first boot a column policy or row policy spelled with another case of such a letter ("CLÉS" for the table "Clés") no longer masks, denies or filters (it fails open), and a grant so spelled no longer grants (it fails closed). Run against the control-plane database: SELECT kind, tenant_id, role, catalog_name, schema_name, table_name, column_name FROM ( SELECT 'grant' AS kind, r.tenant_id, r.name AS role, p.catalog_name, p.schema_name, p.table_name, NULL AS column_name FROM qodstate_role_permission p JOIN qodstate_role r ON r.id = p.role_id UNION ALL SELECT 'column policy', r.tenant_id, r.name, c.catalog_name, c.schema_name, c.table_name, c.column_name FROM qodstate_role_column_policy c JOIN qodstate_role r ON r.id = c.role_id UNION ALL SELECT 'row policy', r.tenant_id, r.name, w.catalog_name, w.schema_name, w.table_name, NULL FROM qodstate_role_row_policy w JOIN qodstate_role r ON r.id = w.role_id ) AS rows WHERE octet_length(concat(catalog_name, schema_name, table_name, column_name)) <> char_length(concat(catalog_name, schema_name, table_name, column_name)) ORDER BY tenant_id, role, kind;

Find every tenant-less account whose kind is not admin (SELECT username, kind FROM qodstate_user WHERE tenant IS NULL AND lower(kind) <> 'admin') and set the kind of each one that should stay a superuser back to admin: such an account loses data access, refused like an unknown user.

Local runtime: list the pools that set cpu or memory (SELECT tenant_db_id, name, cpu, memory FROM qodstate_pool WHERE cpu <> '' OR memory <> '') and clear or resize each one: their nodes now get them as DuckDB threads and memory_limit instead of every core and 80% of the host's memory.
Under HA, finish the rollout before creating staff users: a replica still on an older release reads every staff user as a superuser.

Fleet: upgrade the servers (qod fleet join) with the manager and give every HA replica the same QOD_S3_*: a server on an earlier release does not read the store keys the manager now sends, and a server of this release takes none from an earlier manager. Set QOD_FLEET_NODE_S3_ENDPOINT where servers reach the store at another address than the manager.
Remove QOD_S3_*, QOD_AZURE_* and QOD_GCS_* from every fleet server, which now ignores them, and restart every node so the proxy credential fix and the local pool sizes apply.

Upgrade every manager replica together with its nodes: column and row policies now run only on qod-node (node protocol 10, signed handle version 8), and a node of an earlier protocol refuses this release's handles. The gateway's CLS and RLS rewriting is gone; QOD_CLS_ENABLED=false and QOD_RLS_ENABLED=false remain the kill switches.

Restart every node so it runs DuckDB 2.0.1 and node protocol 10: a node an earlier release started keeps running DuckDB 2.0.0 until it restarts. On Kubernetes that means the new node image; fleet servers need this release's qod fleet join, which bundles the 2.0.1 qod-node. No catalog migrates.

Unset QOD_CLS_ENFORCEMENT, QOD_CLS_UNRESOLVED_TABLE and QOD_RLS_ENFORCEMENT: they were removed and are ignored. Review the native policy limits (docs/node-column-security.md, docs/node-row-security.md): writes to a table a column or row policy covers, view-scoped policies, unsupported column types and unsupported predicates are now refused.

Read the boot output and fix each stderr WARN: line it prints for a row policy naming a column its table no longer has (it now denies every statement reading that table under its role), a stored mask outside the allowed forms, and a stored row predicate or mask the parser read only in part (a predicate so stored now denies its table). Update or delete each policy named.

Check the boot output for column masks that do not return their column's type: qod-node refuses every read of such a column. The manager prints one WARN: line on stderr per such mask and DuckLake database, naming the tenant, the role, the policy id, the column, the mask's type and the column's. Rewrite each with the TRY_CAST form, or use NULL or a deny.

Label the fleet servers before upgrading the manager: a fleet pool's cohort nodeSelector is now honoured, so a cohort's new nodes only go on servers whose labels contain the selector, and a node that restarts or is refilled while no free server carries them goes pending with reason none_match. Start each server with qod fleet join --label key=value (or QOD_FLEET_LABELS). Running nodes are not moved; pools without cohorts are unaffected.

Watch pools whose cohort slots were refilled before the upgrade: such a node's cohort now comes from its id, so when it restarts it may go pending with none_match or take a server of another cohort, for as long as the id lives.
